identification: Georgian-style mahogany ladder (rail) back side chair with drop-in upholstered seat, square tapered legs with stretchers; photo shows modern pale-blue floral seat cover; likely late 18th to early 19th century

entries.venue: Fairford Barn Antiques via Antiques Atlas (UK)
entries.note: English mahogany ladderback side chair c.1790, restored; Armitage chair has plain straight-ish legs and a different back pattern and age unconfirmed. Retail dealer asking, not a sale. aud_price blank rather than converting.

viewing_check: Check whether the joints are tight, seat frame and rails original, any splits at back rails, old repairs, and whether it is 1790s English or a later reproduction.
searches_tried: web: Georgian mahogany rail back side chair auction Australia; ladder back side chair for sale Australia price. Carters results bot-checked and skipped; Shapiro links dead. One UK dealer asking price.
story: Ladder or rail back side chairs in the Hepplewhite style were made in England from the 1770s to the 1800s and were shipped to the colonies; a chair like this may date from that period or be a later copy. Nothing provenance-specific is visible. https://antiques-atlas.com/antique/mahogany_ladderback_chair_circa_1790_a218/as978a218

identification: Unframed acrylic dot painting on stretched canvas, 32x42 cm: a turtle among interlacing red serpents with footprints and meeting-place symbols; reverse inked 'Boomiri Australia' (artist/brand name, not a recognised artist-community name)
viewing_check: Look at the back for a certificate of authenticity, artist name, community or art centre label; absence suggests a tourist-market piece with little resale value.
searches_tried: web: Aboriginal acrylic turtle serpent painting; Boomiri Australia Aboriginal art canvas company; Boomiri Aboriginal painting sold or price turtle. Found nothing about 'Boomiri'; no like-for-like price. Bluethumb comparable page was dead.
story: The back is inked 'Boomiri Australia', which I could not trace to an artist, community or art centre, so I could not verify authorship. The imagery (turtle, serpents, tracks, U-shaped sitting symbols) is standard Western Desert style dot painting, widely produced for the souvenir and gallery trade; no story beyond that verified.

identification: Mid-Victorian cedar chiffonier with inverted shield door panels, c1850, 120 x 117 x 48 cm
viewing_check: Check it is Australian red cedar (not a veneer or mahogany), look for Tasmanian secondary timbers such as Huon pine or blackwood inside, and the condition of the back and feet.
searches_tried: WebSearch: 'Victorian cedar chiffonier Tasmania auction sold colonial cedar c1850 ...'; 'Victorian cedar chiffonier inverted shield panels c1850 sold'. Most results are Carters (bot check, skipped). Leski flipbook page would not load. A Merchant of Welby comparable showed SOLD with no price, so not recorded.
story: Cedar chiffoniers of this shield-panel type were made in the colonies from the 1840s to 1860s; a Merchant of Welby example (1850s, 107 x 122 x 46 cm, shield panel doors, turned columns, full cedar) is a close match in form and size, though sold with no price shown. Source: https://merchantofwelby.com.au/print/australian-furniture/mid-19th-century-colonial-australian-cedar-chiffonier

identification: Birdseye Huon pine framed barometer, H 61 cm (photos not viewable from my environment)
viewing_check: Check the barometer movement/dial maker, whether the Huon pine is solid or veneer, and whether the glass and dial are original.
searches_tried: WebSearch: birdseye huon pine framed barometer Tasmania; huon pine birdseye barometer sold auction; antique aneroid barometer huon pine case; huon pine barometer antique Tasmanian sold OR asking; huon pine history. Results were only Carters (bot check, skipped) or non-comparable furniture; no comparable huon pine barometer price seen on a page.
story: Birdseye Huon pine is a figured form of Tasmania's slow-growing Huon pine, used for colonial-era furniture and picture frames, with Carters listing 19th-century birdseye Huon pine frames and a c1835 Tasmanian bookcase in it. One dealer page says birdseye Huon is a rare timber, sometimes salvaged from drowned hydro-lake logs. Source: https://tasmaniantonewoods.com/blogs/news/birdseye-huon-pine-a-rare-find

identification: Pine railway station bench seat, c1920, L 148 cm (likely a state government railway platform/waiting-room seat)
viewing_check: Look underneath and on the back for stamps, paper labels, inventory numbers or a railway name (Tasmanian Government Railways stamps would add value); check for reversible back, rot at the feet and leg joins.
searches_tried: WebSearch: Tasmanian Government Railways pine railway station bench seat vintage; antique pine railway bench seat c1920 sold auction Australia. Only dealer pages for other benches (Merchant of Welby page is marked SOLD with no price; others UK/US dealers, longer and different). No comparable price recorded.
story: Old Australian government railway benches were commonly made in pine or kauri pine and stamped with government inventory marks; a dealer example dated c1899 by its inventory stamp was a reversible kauri pine seat made by HT Jones, with the maker's paper label underneath. Worth checking this one for similar stamps or labels. Source: https://merchantofwelby.com.au/print/australian-furniture/pair-antique-railway-kauri-pine-bench-seats

identification: Georgian mahogany dropside (drop-leaf/Pembroke-type) table on tapered legs with a drawer, H 72 x W 126 x D 102 cm (presumably leaves up; period and wood not verified)

entries.note: Dealer asking, early 1800s Georgian Cuban mahogany Pembroke drop-side table, frieze drawer, ebony line inlay, tapered turned legs, 108 x 62 x 74 cm closed (118 cm open). Smaller and better-documented than the Armitage table; dealer retail, not a hammer price.

viewing_check: Confirm it is genuinely Georgian (hand-cut dovetails, old secondary timbers, patina) and not a later reproduction; check hinges and rule joints on the leaves, the drawer runners and lock, and any leg repairs or replaced castors.
searches_tried: WebSearch: Georgian mahogany dropside table tapered legs drawer sold hammer 2025; Georgian mahogany Pembroke or dropleaf table with drawer Australia price. Read Bazaa (asking), Merchant of Welby (sold, no price), Roseberys page (no data). No dated sold comparable.
story: Pembroke and drop-side tables like this were the flexible small tables of Georgian dining and parlour rooms, folding down to sit against a wall; Australian dealers sell early 1800s English examples in Cuban mahogany with a frieze drawer and ebony line inlay. Source: https://bazaa.com.au/products/antique-english-georgian-mahogany-drop-side-table

identification: Unframed Aboriginal-style acrylic on canvas titled 'Platypus', H 35 x W 45 cm (artist not identified in catalogue; photos not viewable)
viewing_check: Turn it over and look for the artist's name, community or art-centre label, certificate of authenticity or stamp. Value depends almost entirely on who painted it: an art-centre work by a named artist is worth far more than an unsigned souvenir canvas.
searches_tried: WebSearch: Aboriginal acrylic on canvas platypus painting unframed sold; Aboriginal dot painting platypus Dreaming story. Only retail pages for other artists' platypus paintings (e.g. Chern'ee Sutton at A$1,500 for a much larger 61 x 91 cm work, not comparable, not recorded). No same-artist comparable.
story: Could not identify the artist. As a reference point, contemporary Kalkadoon artist Chern'ee Sutton paints a 'Platypus Dreaming' that portrays the platypus as a gentle waterway traveller, with circles and water patterns for journeys beginning, crossing and returning; whether this lot has any similar meaning is unconfirmed. Source: https://www.cherneesutton.com.au/products/platypus-dreaming-rantani-kalu-ritjinguthinha
